title: The Payroll Verification Trap
subject: URGENT: Verify Your Payroll Details Before 5 PM
scenario:
Dear Employee,

As part of our monthly payroll audit, all employees must verify their bank account information before 5 PM today. Failure to complete this verification may result in a delay to your upcoming salary.

Please use the secure verification portal below. Do not reply to this email as this mailbox is not monitored.

Regards,
Human Resources
email_note: Investigate the sender domain, the difference between the displayed link and its destination, and the pressure created by the deadline.
options: The email uses a non-company sender domain, redirects to a different domain, and threatens salary delays to create urgency.
The email is suspicious only because it was sent before normal office hours.
The sender uses a payroll-related address, which proves the request is genuine.
The email is safe because it does not ask employees to reply with their bank details.
explanation: Three warning signs appear together: the sender domain is not the official company domain, the actual link destination differs from the displayed company address, and the salary-delay threat pressures employees into acting quickly. Verify payroll requests through an independently known HR contact.

title: The Microsoft Sign-in Warning
subject: Your Microsoft 365 Account Will Be Suspended
scenario:
Dear User,

Our security system has detected unusual activity on your Microsoft 365 account. Your account will be suspended within 30 minutes unless you complete the security confirmation process.

Please sign in immediately using the link below to prevent loss of access to company email and files.

IT Support Team
email_note: The sender claims to be IT, but inspect the actual sender address and destination of the sign-in link.
options: The email is suspicious because it uses an external sender domain, creates a 30-minute deadline, and sends users to a non-Microsoft sign-in page.
The email is legitimate because Microsoft accounts can sometimes be suspended.
The only concern is that the email does not include the employee's full name.
The email is safe because it mentions unusual account activity and security.
explanation: Attackers frequently impersonate IT teams and Microsoft security alerts. The external sender, artificial deadline, and fake sign-in destination are multiple warning signs. Never enter company credentials through an unverified link.

title: The Unexpected QR Code
subject: Mandatory MFA Re-registration Required
scenario:
Dear Employee,

We are updating our multi-factor authentication system. All employees must scan the attached QR code to reconnect their company accounts.

Please complete this process today. If the QR code does not work, reply to this email with your current authentication code so that our team can activate your account manually.

Regards,
IT Support
email_note: Even a familiar-looking sender address does not automatically make an unusual security request safe.
options: The request asks employees to scan an unexpected QR code and disclose an authentication code, which could allow an attacker to access their account.
The message is suspicious only because it contains an image attachment.
The request is safe because the sender uses the company's email domain.
The only issue is that employees are asked to complete the process on the same day.
explanation: Unexpected QR codes can redirect users to fake sign-in pages. Authentication codes must never be shared with anyone, including someone claiming to be IT. Confirm unexpected MFA changes through the official IT support channel. A familiar sender address alone is not proof of authenticity.

title: The Courier Delivery Document
subject: Failed Office Delivery – Action Required
scenario:
Dear Recipient,

A package addressed to your office could not be delivered because the delivery details were incomplete.

Please open the attached delivery document to confirm your address and reschedule the shipment. The document contains the required instructions.

Failure to respond within 24 hours may result in the package being returned.

Delivery Operations
options: The sender is unverified, the delivery claim is unexpected, and the spreadsheet contains macro-enabled content that should not be opened without verification.
The email is safe because delivery companies commonly send tracking documents.
The only concern is the 24-hour response deadline.
The attachment is safe because Excel files are standard office documents.
explanation: An unexpected delivery notification, an unverified sender, and a macro-enabled spreadsheet create a suspicious combination. Macro-enabled files can execute malicious code. Verify the shipment independently before opening attachments.

title: The CEO's Confidential Request
subject: Confidential – Immediate Assistance Required
scenario:
Hello,

I am currently attending an important external meeting and cannot take calls. I need you to purchase gift cards for a client appreciation activity immediately.

Purchase the cards using your personal payment method and send me the redemption codes by email. I will arrange reimbursement later.

Please keep this confidential until the client announcement is made.

Regards,
Managing Director
options: The sender uses an unverified executive identity, requests personal spending, asks for gift card redemption codes, and demands secrecy.
The email is legitimate because senior management sometimes makes urgent requests.
The only suspicious detail is that the sender cannot take calls.
The request is safe because reimbursement has been promised.
explanation: This is a common executive impersonation and gift-card scam. Requests for personal payments, redemption codes, secrecy, and urgent action should be independently verified through a known management contact.

title: The Shared Project Document
subject: A Document Has Been Shared With You
scenario:
Hello,

A colleague has shared an updated project budget document with you. The document requires your review before the project meeting.

To view the document, sign in using your company email and password through the access portal below.

The document will be removed automatically if you do not access it today.
email_note: Check whether the sender is a known colleague, whether the destination matches the displayed address, and whether the deadline is genuine.
options: The sender is an unfamiliar external address, the displayed and actual link domains differ, and the removal deadline pressures the recipient.
The email is safe because employees regularly share project documents.
The only warning sign is that the document is related to a project budget.
The email is genuine because it displays an Office-related link.
explanation: Fake shared-document notifications often steal company credentials. An unfamiliar sender, mismatched link destination, and artificial deadline make this suspicious. Confirm with the colleague through a trusted communication channel.

title: The Vendor Bank Account Change
subject: Important: Updated Bank Details for Future Payments
scenario:
Dear Accounts Team,

We have recently changed our banking partner. Please update our payment details before processing the pending invoice.

The new account details are mentioned in the attached document. Kindly ensure all future payments are transferred to the new account immediately.

Please do not use the old bank details after today.

Regards,
ABC Industrial Supplies
options: The email changes payment instructions, provides new bank details through an attachment, and requests immediate use without independent verification.
The email is safe because vendors are allowed to change their banking partners.
The only concern is that the new bank details are attached as a PDF.
The request can be accepted if the invoice amount matches the purchase order.
explanation: Business email compromise often involves fraudulent bank-account changes. Even if the vendor name and invoice appear genuine, independently verify the change using a previously registered phone number or trusted contact before transferring money.

title: The Duplicate Invoice Pressure
subject: Urgent: Pending Invoice – Second Payment Required
scenario:
Dear Accounts Team,

The supplier has informed us that payment for invoice INV-2481 has not been received. They have requested another transfer today to avoid suspension of material delivery.

Please process the payment again using the attached invoice. We will reconcile the earlier transaction later.

Regards,
Finance Coordination
options: The email requests a second payment without confirming the first transaction, uses delivery pressure, and skips reconciliation.
The request is safe because the supplier has sent an invoice copy.
The only suspicious point is the use of the word urgent in the subject.
The payment should be repeated because delivery delays can affect business operations.
explanation: Duplicate-payment fraud can exploit pressure from suppliers or impersonated finance staff. Check payment records, invoice numbers, and supplier confirmations before processing another transfer. Never bypass normal reconciliation.

title: The Purchase Order Approval Shortcut
subject: Management Approved – Release Purchase Order Immediately
scenario:
Hello Team,

Management has verbally approved the attached purchase order for an urgent equipment requirement.

The usual approval workflow is taking too long, so please release the order directly to the supplier. The formal approval document can be added to the system next week.

Please proceed without waiting for the usual system confirmation.

Regards,
Procurement Operations
options: The request relies on unverified verbal approval, asks employees to bypass the normal workflow, and postpones required documentation.
The request is safe because the procurement department sent it.
The only issue is that the purchase order is marked urgent.
The purchase can proceed because formal approval can always be recorded afterward.
explanation: Fraudsters may impersonate internal teams to bypass purchasing controls. Verbal claims of approval should be independently confirmed, and required purchase authorization must be completed before releasing an order.

title: The Employee Salary Account Update
subject: Employee Bank Account Update – Process Before Payroll Closure
scenario:
Dear Payroll Team,

An employee has requested an urgent change to their salary bank account. The updated account details are attached.

The employee is currently unavailable to confirm the request, but the change must be completed before payroll closure today.

Please update the payroll system based on the attached information to avoid salary processing delays.

Regards,
Payroll Administration
options: The sender uses a non-company domain, the employee has not independently confirmed the change, and the request pressures payroll to bypass verification.
The request is safe because payroll teams regularly update employee bank accounts.
The only concern is that the employee is temporarily unavailable.
The change should be accepted because the account details are provided in a spreadsheet.
explanation: Payroll diversion fraud attempts to redirect employee salaries into accounts controlled by criminals. Confirm employee identity and bank-account changes using the approved HR/payroll verification process before updating records.
